From: Prof. Emma Li <emma.li@redwood.edu>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Inquiry: Education & nonprofit pricing for research lab + partner org

Hi Marissa,

I lead the Cognitive Systems Lab at Redwood University. We're piloting a course-integrated research project that will run hosted API workloads for student projects (classroom) and a small ongoing research pipeline (non-prod research). We also partner with Sacred Horizons, a local nonprofit, to deploy a public-facing assistant for resource navigation.

Our questions:
- Do you offer an education discount for university research & course usage?
- What proof of affiliation is required?
- Is there a separate nonprofit/charity pricing path for Sacred Horizons and what verification do you need?
- Given tight grant budgets, is Redwood open to a baseline rate exception or capped pilot pricing for the first 3 months?

Estimated first-quarter usage: ~15M input tokens + 25M output tokens (mixed short prompts + generation). We need something budgetable for a grant application and a statement we can include for procurement.

I've attached our lab affiliation letter and a draft MOU with Sacred Horizons. Happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Emma
Prof. Emma Li
Cognitive Systems Lab
Redwood University
Attachments: edu_affiliation.pdf (PDF, 120KB), SacredHorizons_MOU_draft.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Prof. Emma Li <emma.li@redwood.edu>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-03T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Education & nonprofit pricing for research lab + partner org

Hi Emma — great to meet you via email and thanks for the context. I'm copying Monica from Revenue Operations to keep procurement in the loop.

Short answers up front:
- Education discount: yes — we offer an education pricing program for qualifying university labs and teaching programs. Standard hosted API list rates can be discounted for academic use; typical academic research discounts range from 30–50% depending on scope and whether usage is course-based vs. production-facing.
- Nonprofit: we have a charitable pricing program for verified 501(c)(3)-equivalents. Discounts there are typically more aggressive (up to 60% off list) for small orgs doing public-benefit work.
- Proof: .edu email + affiliation letter OR a letter from the department on letterhead; for nonprofits we need a 501(c)(3) determination letter or equivalent.
- Baseline exception / pilot: we can approve short-term pilot pricing to fit grant cycles; options include a temporary capped per-token pilot rate or a one-time credit applied to the account.

To be concrete given your numbers: with your 3-month pilot estimate (~40M tokens total), I can propose an internal starter offer: up to 45% off list for the hosted API for 90 days OR a $7,500 pilot credit plus the standard education discount (whichever nets more savings). We'll treat Sacred Horizons separately but can do a bundled review if you want both under a shared billing arrangement.

Next steps I need from you to progress this:
1) Confirm whether the grant requires a written rate/quote on company letterhead (we can provide).
2) Attach the lab affiliation/department letter (the .edu doc you mentioned is ideal).
3) If you want Sacred Horizons priced under Redwood's nonprofit program, have them provide their 501(c)(3) doc or equivalent; we've put a checklist in the procurement step below.

If you prefer, we can also book a 30-minute call this week to walk through the quote and pilot terms. Happy to jump on calendar — tell me times that work.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Mid-Market
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: none

Best,
